key_insight: Better web agents need targeted practice in reusable skills, not just more tasks. MiniWeb makes it possible to identify which interaction skills fail instead of measuring only overall task success.
problem_solved: Task-level success scores can hide the specific weaknesses that prevent browser agents from reliably navigating, searching, and completing transactions.
method: Build MiniWeb: a realistic miniature web with 65 interconnected websites across 15 domains.
Provide 369 human-annotated tasks representing everyday web workflows.
Label 37 reusable interaction primitives across 7 skill families to support skill-level diagnosis.
impact: AI practitioners can use skill-level evaluation to pinpoint agent weaknesses and prioritize targeted training. The supplied abstract is truncated, so comparative benchmark results are not available.
visual_elements: Network map of 65 websites, color-coded by their 15 domains.
Skill hierarchy showing 7 families branching into 37 interaction primitives.
Example workflow annotated with the skills required at each step.
Conceptual comparison of a single task-success score with a detailed skill-level diagnostic.
paper_title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
paper_authors: Minh Pham-Dinh, Md Farhan Ishmam, Hernan Yupanqui, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Kenneth Marino
